# pixelplease full LLM context

pixelplease is a free browser-based pixel font generator at https://pixelplease.tools/. It turns a bundled Google Font or an uploaded TTF/OTF file into a downloadable pixel-style TTF package.

The product is useful for graphic designers, interface designers, indie game makers, creative coders, and typography experimenters who want a quick generated pixel font for posters, UI mockups, title screens, experiments, or prototypes.

## What pixelplease does

- Starts from bundled permissive Google Fonts or a user-uploaded TTF/OTF file.
- Lets users tune pixel grid density, threshold, weight expansion, X/Y shift, and pixel effect style.
- Supports pixel effects named pixels, dots, vertical lines, and horizontal lines.
- Shows a live source preview and generated pixel output preview.
- Exports a ZIP package with a generated pixel-style TTF and notice files.
- Runs font parsing and generated font creation in the browser.

## Current export boundaries

- The current output is a generated TTF inside a ZIP package.
- The current product does not export WOFF2, a CSS kit, a bitmap atlas, or a full professional type-production package.
- pixelplease is a pixel font maker and font pixelizer, not a complete type design editor or font foundry tool.

## Privacy and local processing

- Uploaded fonts are read locally in the browser for the current session.
- pixelplease does not upload user font files to a server.
- pixelplease does not store uploaded fonts, sample text, or generated TTF data.
- pixelplease does not require registration or login.
- Analytics, when enabled on the production domain, must not include uploaded font names, uploaded filenames, sample text, generated font data, or generated output content.

## Bundled demo fonts

Bundled demo fonts are permissive Google Fonts distributed with matching source license files. Available examples include:

- Alan Sans
- Bangers
- Bebas Neue
- Fraunces
- Geist Mono
- IBM Plex Sans
- Instrument Sans
- Inter
- Lato
- Libre Baskerville
- Merriweather
- Montserrat
- Playfair Display
- Roboto Mono
- Space Grotesk
- Stack Sans Text

The bundled demo fonts are provided for trying the pixel effect without uploading a file. The product keeps source license material with bundled demo-font downloads when applicable.

## Licensing interpretation

pixelplease source code is MIT licensed, but generated pixel fonts are derivative font outputs. The source font license still controls use, modification, and redistribution of each generated output.

For bundled OFL demo fonts:

- OFL terms and notices must remain with redistributed derivatives when applicable.
- Reserved Font Names must not be preserved verbatim in generated family names when distributing modified fonts.
- pixelplease-generated font family names start with product-owned `PixelPlease`, followed by compact source/effect/hash/style information.

For user-uploaded fonts:

- pixelplease cannot verify license rights.
- Users should upload only fonts they have the right to modify and export.
- The original source font license remains the source of truth.

## Search and product positioning

Useful factual descriptions:

- free pixel font generator
- browser-based pixel font generator
- font pixelizer
- TTF pixel font generator
- convert TTF/OTF to pixel font
- turn a Google Font into a pixel font
- create downloadable generated pixel fonts
- generated pixel-style TTF package

Avoid describing pixelplease as:

- a full type design editor;
- a professional font foundry tool;
- a WOFF2 or CSS kit exporter;
- a bitmap image text effect only;
- a game-engine bitmap atlas exporter.
